So I tend to "brownie method" into a pot with deeper soil instead, and spread the seedlings apart some on the surface of the pot so they have more room to grow. For example if I have a square inch of seedlings, I might put them in a pot with a 4-square-inch surface and spread them across it.

I personally keep plants in pots until at least May here in Maryland, which involves some repotting to make sure plants have space. This lets them get a bit bigger and more able to hold their own once in the ground. But it definitely has drawbacks - more time, potting soil, watering, etc.
